items.summary:
A Siemens report estimates unplanned downtime costs an average large plant in the surveyed sectors $253 million per year. NVIDIA's Factory Operations Blueprint (FOX) offers a reference architecture for adding a long-running factory manager agent to existing systems, coordinating specialized agents that inspect defects, arrange rework, and investigate causes using real-time data from databases, MES, and ERP systems. At Siemens' Erlangen electronics plant, the approach can enable cost savings of up to 20% in production planning and reduce time to market by up to 40% for new designs via virtual prototypes and synthetic training data. The SMT reference example traces an AOI alert through inspection, rework, and root cause analysis without requiring manual queries across systems.

visual null
items.title: NVIDIA Blueprint Lets Factory Agents Investigate Defects and Coordinate Rework

items.summary: This tutorial walks through a complete agent-optimization cycle using NVIDIA NeMo tools, following the NemoClaw blueprint. It explains that generic benchmark scores may not explain an agent's failures, which can include wrong tool calls or missed requirements. The process uses recorded traces analyzed by NeMo Compass to build a prioritized backlog of issues, then creates tests with NeMo Eval Author and updates the harness accordingly. In one example involving Dassault Systèmes' LEO engineering assistant, fixing misplaced arguments reduced malformed tool calls from 142 to zero. A separate door design workflow showed about a 28% relative improvement in evaluation score and 35% fewer tool calls per run across six scenarios over roughly 12 hours, with no reported regressions.
items.title: NVIDIA NeMo Compass Turns Agent Failures Into Tests and Fixes

items.summary: On November 4, 2026, Ai2 announced a new climate modeling initiative backed by multimillion-dollar, three-year funding from Google.org and technical support from Google Research. The project will develop NeuralGCM+, an open-source model extending the existing NeuralGCM to simulate atmosphere and ocean together for long-term projections spanning years to decades. While conventional models limit large-scale experiments due to computational demands—illustrated by a public benchmark where an atmosphere-only version simulated a full year globally in eight minutes on one TPU, and Ai2’s ACE2 ran climate studies roughly 100 times faster than the model it emulated—the new effort aims for more reliable regional forecasts. Ai2 plans three fronts: connecting atmosphere and ocean, improving responses to warming climates, and making tools easier to use. The initiative targets scientists worldwide, with particular relevance to regions such as the southwestern United States facing changing rainfall and water availability through mid-century.
items.title: Ai2 and Google Partner on Next-Generation Climate Models

items.summary: Google announced that schools banning all AI will lose access to Google Search, according to Chris Phillips, vice-president for education at Google. Speaking to the New York Times, he said search and AI are deeply integrated, so students would see a message indicating unavailability. Given Google's roughly 91% global market share across devices, the move is significant for US students.
items.title: Google To Cut Search Access For Schools That Ban AI

items.summary: A writer tested Apple's new Siri Recaps feature, available in the first developer beta of iOS 27.3 and watchOS 27.3 released Tuesday. The AI-powered audio recording and summarization on Apple Watch Series 12 automatically saves notes from conversations around the wearer. While sound and song detection raise no privacy concerns since they process on-device without identifying speakers, Live Rewind and Siri Recaps record transcribed or summarized conversations, which some find unsettling as technology normalizes constant listening. The writer found value in capturing details spoken too fast to note manually during a car-repair visit yesterday but flagged that recaps mixed unrelated topics together.
items.title: Apple's Siri Recaps Tested as Useful but Unsettling

items.summary: Google drew swift backlash on Tuesday after announcing that schools using its K-12 software will lose access to Search unless they opt in to AI tools. Chris Phillips, Google's vice president for education, told The New York Times the two features are deeply integrated and students would see a message indicating search is unavailable if their school does not opt in. Senator Bernie Sanders called it extortion on X, while Senators Richard Blumenthal and Lina Khan condemned the move as anticompetitive, arguing an unregulated monopolist should not control essential services.
items.title: Google Faces Backlash Over Search Shutdown for Schools Using AI Tools

items.summary: A lead manager memo seen by Reuters reported that Meta Platforms sold its first euros-denominated bonds on Nov 4, raising €9 billion (S$13 billion). The multi-tranche sale had maturities ranging from four to 38 years. Citi and Morgan Stanley were the bookrunners.
items.title: Meta sells first euro bonds, raising €9 billion

items.summary: Dharma-AI released the DharmaOCR-LITE v1.1 model, a 2-billion-parameter field extractor that returns structured JSON from document images. In a benchmark of 546 documents across three request scenarios (1,638 total cases), it scored 0.834 on field-level F1—above every general-purpose frontier configuration tested, which ranged from Claude Opus 5 at 0.816 to GPT-5.6 Luna at 0.741. Running self-hosted on a single L40S GPU at $2.24 per hour, it is roughly six times lower cost than GPT-5.6 Luna and up to 147 times lower than GPT-5.6 Sol. The authors frame this as evidence that specialized small models can outperform frontier APIs on bounded tasks.
items.title: Dharma-AI's Field Extractor Beats Frontier LLMs on Cost and Accuracy

items.summary: Google announced Tuesday that schools using its software must opt into artificial intelligence or lose access to Google search, since the two are integrated. The change reverses an August default and follows backlash from educators and parents over Gemini in classrooms. Chris Phillips said schools should control AI use; critics called it coercion of a monopoly.
items.title: Google Threatens Search Access for Schools Rejecting AI

items.summary: Since mid-August 2026, a phishing operation dubbed Operation CloudFire has harvested live Google sessions from corporate users by hijacking Google Calendar invites. Material Security’s Threat Research team identified the campaign and took down hundreds of domains. The attacker runs a reverse proxy in front of the genuine sign-in page, relaying SMS, authenticator codes, number matching, and account recovery to bypass second-factor controls. Over one month, Material recorded 68,676 messages blocked, 2,112 unique malicious URLs analyzed, 897 domains taken down, and 8,570 compromised sender addresses across 6,354 root domains—figures drawn only from customers who shared data, so true totals are higher. Material notes the operator has built an unfinished Microsoft 365 branch but appears to have dispersed activity. The full breakdown is in a companion whitepaper.
items.title: Material Security Tackles Google Calendar Phishing Campaign

items.summary: US stocks rose on Nov 4 as investors bet a divided Washington could limit sharp policy shifts, though data centre stocks fell amid concerns over tighter AI regulation. The Dow gained 1,203.07 points to 52,989.79, the S&P 500 added 129.88 points to 7,698.80 and the Nasdaq Composite rose 540.38 points to 25,912.39. Among hyperscalers, Amazon.com jumped 7.1%, Meta Platforms added 1.6% and Alphabet gained 3.4%. Elon Musk-led SpaceX and Tesla were among laggards, down 1.9% and 3.9%. Citi’s Scott Chornert said “the uncertainty related to the elections is now behind us” and warned that slowing data centre buildout could change fundamentals for suppliers.
items.title: Wall Street rallies after Democrats win Congress; data centre stocks slide

items.summary: Lula's campaign accused Meta of electoral interference while its most effective organizing tool was a WhatsApp channel, Exército do Lula. The channel reached 10.5 million followers by October 23 and became the second largest in Brazil; two days later Lula won 51.79% of the vote. Folha de S.Paulo obtained internal messages showing Meta employees acknowledged temporary restrictions harmed Lula's Instagram accounts and that the platform recommended Flávio Bolsonaro's profile, though no employee admitted interference. On October 15, TSE Justice Marco Aurélio Bellizze barred Meta from unequal reach reductions under a BRL 500,000 daily fine; the full court upheld it unanimously the next day. Tech Policy Press authors argue suspicion of bias became a mobilizing weapon running on Meta's servers. The article calls for independent audits and digital sovereignty across Brazil's electoral cycle.
items.title: Brazil's Election Campaign Relied on Meta While Accusing It of Bias

items.summary: Knight-Georgetown Institute executive Alissa Cooper explains what the new AI training opt-out means, noting that last week Google, Microsoft, Anthropic and OpenAI announced support for a mechanism letting publishers opt out of having content used to train models. The proposal was authored by Anthropic’s Kevin Kelley but carries no official IETF status as an individual draft published on October 30 (the “policy token draft”). Cooper highlights three limitations: it is not yet standardized, though providers have committed support by 2027; it covers only AI training while search and inference remain undefined or contested; and EU AI Act signatories are not required to recognize it. She urges the standards process to run before large companies set web rules.
items.title: AI Training Opt-Out Proposal Lacks Search Coverage and Formal Status

items.summary: The Humanitarian Organization for Migration Economics (HOME) wrote to the Ministry of Manpower following a report that MOM probes 45 firms involved in Changi Airport operations for work pass offences. HOME has raised concerns since 2025 about Employment Pass applications used to circumvent Work Permit quotas and levies, deploying holders into low-paid sectors such as parcel delivery, cleaning, and food and beverage services. The group says affected workers should recover unpaid salaries rather than face repatriation, and urges MOM to distinguish employers from deceived workers.
items.title: HOME urges MOM enforcement reform for deceived work-pass workers

items.summary: The National Library & Archives Board replied to a letter from Ryan Joshua Mahindapala urging safeguards for its honour-based check-ins. Assistant Chief Executive Ong Bee Lee said the system is deliberately self-motivated and will consider his suggestions as features are refined, while launching a CrowdTask SG survey before year-end to gather feedback on participants’ reading motivations.
items.title: NLB Responds To ReadSG Challenge Letter

items.summary: Anthropic describes building Scion, a source control system designed for the scale of its coding agents and infrastructure workloads. The article reports that merged changes grew from roughly 2500 per day in May 2026 to more than 30000 per day by September, while main branch history is close to 100 GB and a compressed working copy exceeds 25 GB. Its CI system performs approximately 25 million checkouts per day before counting developer environments, agent sandboxes, and research jobs; a naive transfer approach could generate more than 600 PB of traffic daily. Anthropic explains that Git’s local independence is costly for its mostly automated clients, so Scion shifts repository operations to the server while clients keep only limited caches. It uses changesets, content-addressed immutable objects, shared caching layers, and strict cache boundaries to distribute code quickly across many consumers.
items.title: Anthropic Builds Scion To Handle Source Control For Its Coding Agents

items.summary: Two readers respond to a Jeanette Winterson interview on AI, arguing there is no inevitable dystopia. One compares her point about well-rounded people to Isaac Asimov's 1959 story Profession; the other speculates that superior AI could help solve climate catastrophe and prevent war. Both quote Winterson saying 'there is no inevitable dystopia'.
items.title: Reader links Winterson's AI optimism to Asimov story

items.summary: French authorities say medical fridges used to store donated blood were impacted by recent cyber-attacks from unknown hackers, joining supermarkets already targeted in Europe. The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said cold rooms storing blood had their temperatures set to rise but staff intervened; no health impact has been identified and no loss of blood products is expected. While Russian hacktivist groups have claimed responsibility, analysts question the link, with Iranian actors or even teenagers considered possible. Sekoia reported evidence aligning with Russian activity but said it could be automatic scanning.
items.title: French blood storage hit by freezer cyber-attacks

items.summary: A midterm night that NBC News framed as a backlash against data centers saw Democrats win several high-profile races, including Sherrod Brown in Ohio and upsets for Republicans branded “Data Center Derek” and “DC Derrick.” Voters who favored stricter rules or moratoriums won across federal and gubernatorial contests. Nearly two-thirds of respondents said the issue was at least a minor factor in their vote. Strategists linked voter anger to energy, noise, pollution and Big Tech influence concerns. Democrats routed Republicans despite large industry spending on opponents, including $1.5 million from Building the Future in South Carolina and Kansas. Ballot measures across nine states rejected construction plans or approved pauses. Greg Casar called it an early tremor of a larger shift; Sacha Haworth described it as corruption, affordability and Big Tech influence stories voters understood.
items.title: The Results Are In: Voters Hate Data Centers

items.summary: A first-of-its-kind global “roadmap” produced by Brazil, host of COP30 in Belém, sets out a voluntary plan for countries to move away from coal, oil and gas. It rejects a one-size-fits-all approach, asking nations to diagnose their own readiness before pursuing tailored levers culminating by 2033 – 10 years after the COP28 call. The roadmap introduces a “Belém readiness index” sorting countries into four archetypes across three phases (to 2028, 2030 and 2033). It acknowledges overshooting 1.5C may be needed and frames transition as partly economic. Civil society broadly welcomed it; its uptake at COP31 remains uncertain.
items.title: Brazil unveils voluntary global roadmap for ending fossil fuels

items.summary: Democrats won a majority in Tuesday's midterm elections, capping at least 54 seats while Alaska and Mississippi races stayed undecided, per Bloomberg. The result constrains President Trump's ability to confirm Fed governors. Elizabeth Warren is expected to chair the Banking Committee that oversees the central bank; she would replace Tim Scott. Economist Mark Spindel called a Democratic Senate 'a stronger bulwark,' while Michael Strain of the American Enterprise Institute described it as only 'a marginal reduction in the threat.' The Fed held its benchmark rate steady at 3.
items.title: Democratic Senate Control Bolsters Federal Reserve Independence Prospects

items.summary: A buying guide presents five foldable smartphone picks from Samsung, Google, vivo and Apple, comparing displays, cameras, processors, battery life and features. Prices reach ₹2.99 lakh, with some models near ₹3 lakh. The article asks whether the higher cost is worth it before recommending readers watch its complete guide.
items.title: Top Foldable Phones in India Compared Across Brands and Features

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India dismissed viral claims that ₹10, ₹20 and ₹50 notes might run short during the festive season. A WhatsApp message presented as an RBI advisory suggested new-note availability could be affected before Diwali, raising concern among consumers and small traders. The central bank said sufficient banknotes of all denominations remain available in its vaults and currency chests.
items.title: RBI Rejects Viral Shortage Claims Ahead of Diwali

items.summary: Using daily firm-to-firm transaction data from a large Indian state during the March 2020 COVID-19 lockdowns, Khanna, Morales, and Pandalai-Nayar find that supply chains built on complex inputs and large, well-connected suppliers held up better than those relying on easily replaced ones. Firms with more supplier exposure cut links faster, fell production by as much as 34%, and shifted toward larger, closer suppliers afterward. The authors caution the classification of districts into red zones may not reflect industrial structure, though balance tests support it. Their findings suggest diversification for its own sake buys little resilience in developing economies.
items.title: India's Lockdowns Revealed What Makes Supply Chains Resilient

items.summary: Rohini Pande joined VoxDev to discuss the state of international development, drawing on the introductory chapter she co-edited for Handbook of Development Economics Volume 6. The handbook gathers reviews of major field developments across persistent barriers, aggregate trends and microeconomic foundations. Listed drafts may differ from final chapters; the full version is available by purchase or subscription.
items.title: VoxDev webinar explores state of international development with Rohini Pande

items.summary: US stocks surged after investors digested Democratic victories in the midterm elections, with hopes that Donald Trump’s turbulent policymaking would be restrained. The Dow Jones rose 2%, while the tech-heavy Nasdaq and benchmark S&P 500 each gained more than 1%. Overnight futures had initially pointed to lower markets amid fears over AI companies’ prospects. Meanwhile, the US dollar fell against major trading partners’ currencies to a one-month low on Wednesday as bond yields dropped; the yield on the benchmark 10-year treasury slid 4.7 basis points to 4.918%. Analysts noted that Democrats secured Senate seats in traditional Republican strongholds such as Texas and South Carolina, while gold rose past $4,000 an ounce amid safe-haven demand.
items.title: US Stocks Rise, Dollar Slides After Democrats Win Midterms

items.summary: Governor-elect Gina Hinojosa pledged a moratorium on data center approvals, plunging Texas' booming industry into uncertainty after she defeated Greg Abbott. Big Tech firms have major projects in the state, and ERCOT tracked over 400 gigawatts seeking grid connection. Rural opposition helped her win; polls showed strong voter support for limits. Hinojosa vows to protect communities as decisions shift from federal to local control.
items.title: Hinojosa's Data Center Crackdown Casts Shadow Over Texas Industry

items.summary: According to Nikkei, Japan plans to seek earlier access to undisclosed software vulnerability information from US AI developers and other overseas technology firms as it strengthens defences against rising cyberattacks. The government may present an emergency cybersecurity package at a ministerial meeting possibly convened Friday. Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi instructed officials in late October to devise steps following increased attacks.
items.title: Japan Plans Access to US AI Firms' Vulnerability Data Amid Cyberattacks

items.summary: A small alligator entered Bagel Dock Express in North Carolina, moving from the back room into the main dining area and frightening employees. The incident is captured on video posted online.
items.title: Alligator strolls into North Carolina bagel shop

items.summary: The conservative group Alliance for a Better Future, led by former Virginia official Janet Kelly, argues in a post-midterms memo that Super Intelligence policy helped deliver Democratic majorities and urges Republicans to recalibrate before the 2028 presidential election. The memo warns that ignoring AI’s economic ties was political malpractice and recommends guardrails beyond Trump’s light-touch agenda.
items.title: Conservative AI Group Urges Republicans to Recalibrate

items.summary: The article reports that most current AI investment targets enterprise applications, while noting that major tech successes have historically begun with consumers. Marissa Mayer of the consumer app Dazzle stated on Semafor's Future Proof podcast that she expects consumer AI to reach about twice the size of enterprise by 2030. She describes Dazzle as an assistant built from a user's photo reel, calling it a preview of an arriving wave.
items.title: Marissa Mayer Forecasts Consumer AI Wave by 2030

items.summary: Canadians welcomed a Democratic sweep in Tuesday's US midterm election, which Ontario Premier Doug Ford called 'a victory for Canada' and saw as hope for relief from Donald Trump's tariffs on close trade allies. However, the article notes that near-term tariff relief is unlikely, since Trump has enacted his levies through executive orders rather than Congress, giving him veto power over new bills. Canadian officials remain cautious: Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said Canada's approach would not change and dismissed speculation about a new Democratic Congress as 'an interesting discussion at a faculty club luncheon.' While some see leverage in the unpopular tariffs, others caution that Trump may be distracted by investigations before any deal is finalised between now and January.
items.title: Canadian Optimism After Democratic Midterm Sweep Amid Tariff Talks

items.summary: Ukraine police released bodycam footage showing residents of the southern village of Kamyshuvakha moving to an underground shelter before a second Russian bomb strike. The double-tap attack killed at least 40 people across an aid centre and a shelter, Ukraine said. President Volodymyr Zelensky stated that nine aerial bombs were dropped by Russia while rescuers responded, and that more than 30 people may still be under the rubble as searches continued for a third day. The Russian military has not publicly commented.
items.title: Ukraine Releases Bodycam Footage of Deadly Russian Bombing in Kamyshuvakha

items.summary: The New York attorney general, Letitia James, appointed former federal prosecutor Jacqueline Kelly as outside counsel to lead a criminal investigation into 2024 sexual assault allegations at Cornell University. Kelly will report directly to James’s office and examine all available evidence in the reopened case involving seven fraternity members accused of drugging and assaulting a student over seven hours in October 2024, which drew public backlash after no arrests followed Doe’s civil lawsuit.
items.title: New York AG Appoints Former Prosecutor to Lead Cornell Assault Probe

items.summary: In the US midterm elections, Democrats won control of both the Senate and the House as a wave of Republican defeats swept through states once considered safe. James Talarico became Texas’s first Democratic senator since 1988 after defeating attorney general Ken Paxton, while Abdul El-Sayed made history as the country’s first Muslim senator in Michigan. In Kansas, Adam Hamilton won his state’s Senate seat for the first time in 94 years; Annie Andrews flipped South Carolina to a Democrat for the first time since 1998; and Susan Collins conceded her Maine seat after nearly three decades. Hakeem Jeffries is poised to become the first Black speaker of the House, declaring “America is back. ” The incoming Democratic majority plans to use oversight powers aggressively against Trump’s conduct, challenge his tariffs, rein in ICE deportations, and block judicial appointments, though it will likely face a 60-vote filibuster on major legislation.
items.title: Democrats Win Control of Congress in Midterm Blue Wave

items.summary: EL PAÍS reports that Tuesday's midterm elections marked a historic surge for the American left, with at least five candidates backed by the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) winning congressional and local executive races. The article frames this as a 'socialist summer' sparked partly by Zohran Mamdani's New York campaign, noting DSA influence in Washington is expected to grow next year. Political science professor Grant Davis Reeher told EL PAÍS the results raise questions about democratic socialism's place within the Democratic Party but offer no definitive answer. The piece profiles several winners—Claire Valdez (83.08%), Rashida Tlaib (84.78%) and Darializa Ávila Chevalier (88.27%)—while noting some figures like Abdul El-Sayed are not DSA members. Reeher argues Democrats have the board set for 2028 but must still decide their strategy, asking whether leftists can ultimately influence policy outcomes.
items.title: DSA-Backed Leftists Sweep Midterm Ballot Box in Historic Wave

items.summary: On Wednesday, November 4, European leaders voiced hopes for a reset with the United States after voters delivered what was described as a huge defeat to President Donald Trump and his Republican party in the midterms. The report is attributed to FRANCE 24's Dave Keating.
items.title: European leaders welcome Democrats' US midterm win

items.summary: As Shanghai hosts the ninth China International Import Expo from November 5 to 10, an interview on The Hub features Wang Guan speaking with Rogier Janssens, president of Merck China. He discusses Merck's long-term investment strategy in China, its engagement with the country's innovation ecosystem, and the growing role of AI in biotechnology and cancer treatment as part of China's high-quality development.
items.title: Merck China's Long-Term Investment and Innovation Strategy at CIIE

items.summary: The killing of Arlinda Zekaj, a 49-year-old woman in the village of Vitomirica near Peja on October 25, has triggered widespread protests across Kosovo. She had repeatedly asked police for protection against threats from her husband and brother-in-law Albert Sylaj before being murdered with an axe; officers arrived at 9:10 p.m. to find only her body. The incident was the eighth femicide in Kosovo this year, prompting demands that responsible officials be prosecuted and Interior Minister Xhelal Svecla and Justice Minister Donika Gervalla resign. Activist Liridona Sijarina called for criminal accountability across all levels of responsibility. Since 2010, 55 women have been killed by partners or family members in the country.
items.title: Kosovo Protests After Woman Killed Despite Repeated Police Appeals

items.summary: On Tuesday, 55 graduates of the Escola de Papai Noel do Brasil in Rio de Janeiro marked their completion beneath Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado. The free course requires men aged 50 and over with naturally white or grey hair and beards, and covers acting, diction, costume and Brazilian Sign Language. Founded in 1993 by actors Limachem Cherem and Conrado Freitas with designer Fátima Tavares Cherem, the school has trained more than 1,000 Santas over 33 years, along with about 300 Noeletes.
items.title: Santa Claus School graduates at Christ the Redeemer

items.summary: The World Health Organization urges governments to expand six climate and health measures that could prevent an estimated 1.6 million deaths annually, roughly one in every 40 deaths, while delivering major economic benefits, per a new report published Wednesday. WHO Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus said the crisis is largely preventable with existing tools, noting phasing out fossil fuels alone may prevent more than one million premature deaths yearly and yield US$5.4 trillion in fiscal gains.
items.title: WHO Urges Six Climate Actions to Prevent Millions of Deaths

items.summary: Recent drug seizures and laboratory discoveries indicate that Africa is increasingly manufacturing illicit drugs rather than only transiting them. Methamphetamine laboratories have been found in Nigeria, South Africa, Kenya and Mozambique. In 2025, NDLEA dismantled what it called the largest clandestine meth lab ever uncovered there, arresting suspects including three Mexican nationals.
items.title: Africa's Shift from Drug Transit to Production Hub

items.summary: After defeating Mike Rogers in a race split by the Israel-Gaza dispute, Democrat Abdul El-Sayed welcomed President Trump's plan to end roughly $4 billion in annual military aid to Israel. Speaking after his victory, he said the president is right on this policy and called for stopping arms sales used for genocide and apartheid. He also questioned U.S. support for Egypt, Saudi Arabia, Jordan and Pakistan, urging tax dollars be spent at home.
items.title: El-Sayed Endorses Trump's Israel Aid Cuts After Winning Michigan Senate Seat

items.summary: Libya's eastern-based parliament appointed Fawzi Abu Khazam as Central Bank of Libya governor, accepting the resignation of Naji Issa. According to the parliament's spokesperson, 78 of the 90 members present voted in favour. The east sits under military commander Khalifa Haftar and is divided from a UN-recognised government in Tripoli; the rival High Council of State has not yet commented on the vote.
items.title: Libya's eastern parliament appoints new central bank governor

items.summary: On Tuesday, 55 graduates of Brazil's Escola de Papai Noel do Brasil (Santa Claus School) gathered beneath Christ the Redeemer on Corcovado to mark their training. Dressed in red suits and white beards, they sang carols while riding the mountain railway before a ceremony with a blessing and diploma presentation. The free course runs for a month of Tuesday classes covering acting, diction, costume and Brazilian Sign Language; it was founded in 1993 by actors Limachem Cherem and Conrado Freitas. More than 1,000 Santas have passed through the school over about 33 years, along with roughly 300 Noeletes.
items.title: Brazilian Santa Claus School graduates at Christ the Redeemer

items.summary: Aswath Damodaran, known as the 'Dean of Valuation,' revised his earlier estimate for Anthropic to $1.45 trillion in anticipation of its mega IPO, placing it near the lower end of offering price estimates. He said some market reactions were emotion-driven while others stemmed from cost-of-capital assumptions he views as disconnected from fundamentals. His valuation relies on trailing 12-month revenue and operating income figures that include recently leaked third-quarter numbers. Damodaran cautioned Anthropic faces regulatory, compute-scaling and profitability risks, noting uncertainty is inherent to investing. He outlined four responses—ignore it, avoid it, margin of safety, or law of large numbers—and stressed readers should consult original research before deciding.
items.title: Damodaran Trims Anthropic IPO Valuation Amid Market Pushback

items.summary: Tesla shares fell alongside SpaceX, CoreWeave and Vertiv after investors weighed election results that could reshape the US political environment for tech legislation. Analyst Dan Ives warned Democratic control of the Senate would create hurdles over two years and slow development of 800 to 1,000 planned AI data centers. Texas now raises concerns: Democrat Gina Hinojosa replaced Gov. Greg Abbott, whose moratorium on data centers may continue as a state opposed to expansion could hold up to 25% to 30% of capacity. Musk floated space-based facilities with combined capacity of 1.
items.title: Tesla Shares Fall as Democrats Gain Ground on AI Data Centers

items.summary: A Tata Consultancy Services survey reports that productivity improvement is the leading value from enterprise AI investments, cited by 84 per cent of executives globally. Amit Kapur, TCS Chief AI and Services Transformation Officer, notes security, governance and resilience concerns are holding organisations back. The study also highlights rising risk perceptions in Europe and a shift toward Human+AI operating models with greater autonomy.
items.title: TCS Study Finds Productivity as AI's Top Enterprise Value

items.summary: Elon Musk spent nearly half a billion dollars backing Republican candidates in the midterm elections, hoping to help Republicans keep control of Congress and Texas. Democrats instead won both chambers, Gina Hinojosa defeated Greg Abbott, ending more than three decades of Republican rule in Texas, and Robert Garcia told allies on Tuesday evening: “Lawyer up.” The results pressured Musk’s businesses; Tesla shares fell 3.6% while SpaceX shares dropped 3.2%, even as the S&P 500 rose 1.5%. Analysts expect Democrats to increase scrutiny of data-centre projects, complicating SpaceX plans amid rising electricity costs and local opposition. Trump Media & Technology Group also fell 13.7%. Musk deleted his election-day appeal urging Republican votes.
items.title: Musk's Midterm Bet Backfires as Stocks Slide

items.summary: The Reserve Bank of India announced on Wednesday the formation of a Technical Consultative Committee for Financial Markets (TCCFM) amid rapidly evolving financial markets and infrastructure. The committee, chaired by Deputy Governor Rohit Jain of the RBI’s Financial Markets Regulation Department, will engage market participants on policy and operational matters covering money, government securities, foreign exchange and derivative markets, including efficiency, liquidity, resilience and transaction-cycle issues.
items.title: RBI Forms Financial Markets Committee

items.summary: Global companies said on Wednesday that Democrats' capture of the US Congress is unlikely to ease their near-term outlook amid higher energy and raw-material costs plus a stretched consumer. Some welcomed political stability, but analysts warned tariffs remain in force via executive authority and gridlock could follow. Global stocks rose while chip stocks fell as investors expect more scrutiny of AI.
items.title: Executives See Little Near-Term Relief for Firms After Democratic Win

items.summary: President Donald Trump issued 'The American Declaration of Freedom in Space', asserting US leadership over space exploration, development, use and settlement. Analysts say it ignites a contest to shape new lunar governance rules. Lt Gen AK Bhat (retd), director-general of the Indian Space Association, sees competing frameworks for governing space activities ahead. India must weigh its Artemis ties against 2047 ambitions while safeguarding strategic autonomy.
items.title: Trump's Space Declaration Sparks Moon Rules Contest for India

items.summary: RJD leader Tejashwi Yadav accused the BJP and RSS of targeting his father, Lalu Prasad Yadav, through central agencies. Speaking at a Hyderabad gathering on Wednesday, he said the community draws strength from its association with Lord Krishna. He also condemned preacher Dhirendra Shastri over alleged remarks about Krishna ahead of Uttar Pradesh elections, amid controversy over viral videos.
items.title: Tejashwi Yadav Attacks BJP, RSS Over Krishna Remarks and Harassment of Lalu Prasad

items.summary: Former Indian hockey captain M M Somaya wrote to Karnataka Chief Minister D K Shivakumar after his 1980 Moscow Olympics gold medal was stolen along with three other international medals, ₹30,000 cash and assorted silver items. The burglary occurred in the wee hours of October 28 at his New Thippasandra home while Somaya's family had left for Kodagu around 5 AM on October 25. Neighbouring CCTV footage reportedly showed two unknown persons entering after breaking open the door, prompting police to form two special teams and examine further footage. The total value of stolen items excluding medals is estimated at ₹3.53 lakh.
items.title: Stolen Olympic gold medal prompts complaint from former hockey captain

items.summary: Ramnik Sakhwala, a 39-year-old from Surat who had moved to Russia in 2025 seeking better livelihood opportunities after the local diamond industry slowed down, joined the Russian Army in June 2026 and has not been heard from since. His brother Mahesh told PTI that Ramnik was assured of a non-combat role supplying food to personnel in the war zone, but his family now lacks any confirmation of his status or location. The relatives have approached the Ministry of External Affairs, the Gujarat State Non-Resident Gujaratis Foundation and the Russian Consulate General in Mumbai without receiving concrete answers, while the Indian Embassy says a response may take months or even a year.
items.title: Gujarat Man Vanishes After Joining Russian Army

items.summary: The Punjab government agreed to pay Rs 2 crore compensation and provide a government job for the wife of anti-drug activist Parvinder Singh Jhota, who was shot dead last month. The deal also includes installing a statue, building a trauma centre, withdrawing certain cases, and holding his post-mortem on November 6. Other agreements cover additional compensations to other families.
items.title: Punjab Govt Offers Rs 2 Crore and Job in Jhota Deal

items.summary: A cyberattack on crypto-asset exchange Binance may be the largest theft of its kind on record, with stolen assets estimated at US$6.3 billion (£4.7 billion). On October 29, 2026, analytics firms reported large amounts moved from wallets across multiple blockchains within about 20 minutes. Binance suspended deposits and withdrawals, pledged to cover losses via its emergency protection fund, froze around US$3 billion by October 30, and said it restored 95% of assets as of November 1 — largely from exchange funds rather than recovered thefts. Investigators point to North Korea-linked cybercriminals breaching withdrawal systems, though attribution remains provisional. The author warns the incident highlights custody and governance risks in centralised crypto markets.
items.title: Binance Hack May Be Largest Crypto Theft on Record

items.summary: Melbourne Renegades beat Hobart Hurricanes by four wickets in the Women's Big Bash League on Wednesday, winning through a rare wicketkeeping infringement. Lizelle Lee collected the ball behind the stumps as Deandra Dottin missed the final delivery with scores level at 154. The third umpire called a no-ball under Law 27.3, awarding Renegades the run they needed to avoid a Super Over.
items.title: Rare wicketkeeping no-ball gives Renegades WBBL win over Hurricanes

items.summary: Prem Singh Chandumajra, an Akali leader and former MP, announced on Wednesday his resignation from the Shiromani Akali Dal (Punar Surjit), a breakaway faction led by Giani Harpreet Singh. He said he intends to return to the Badal-led SAD after concluding that his thinking was no longer aligned with Punar Surjit's leadership.
items.title: Akali Leader Resigns From Punar Surjit Faction Ahead of Punjab Polls

items.summary: Eleven SDRF and Fire Services Department personnel went missing Wednesday after two rescue boats capsized while attempting to save five fishermen trapped by a strong current in the overflowing Bethupalli tank in Khammam district, officials said. The team had been stranded when their boat developed a technical snag before proceeding toward the fishermen. Preliminary reports indicate all five fishermen are safe.
items.title: Eleven Rescue Workers Missing After Boats Capsize in Telangana Floods
